solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: At top speed, punctured tyre abroad

parts.note: a tyre that has been punctured is a flat
someone abroad is out of the country, out

explanation.surface: A motorist abroad suffers a puncture while driving at top speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat out is an idiom for going as fast as possible, with maximum effort.

clue.text: Overpraising Cockney milliner in Scottish dance

indicators.note: the milliner is placed in the dance, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the Highland fling is a Scottish dance
a milliner is a hatter; a Cockney drops the H, giving 'atter

explanation.surface: A hat-maker from London's East End is being complimented excessively at a Highland dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, are said to drop their H's, so a hatter becomes 'atter. FLING is the Highland fling, a Scottish dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattering someone means complimenting them excessively or insincerely, which is overpraising.

clue.text: Cause irritation, blowing top in joint

indicators.note: blowing means losing, and the top of a down answer is its first letter, so that letter goes

parts.note: to rankle is to cause lasting irritation

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper over a sore joint that keeps annoying them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowing top' suggests losing one's temper, but here it removes the first letter, R, from RANKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint connecting the foot to the leg.

clue.text: Resort bad? Summon one who looks into complaints

indicators.note: read as re-sort: sort the letters again, putting them in a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint about a poor holiday resort, with a call to summon an official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place but is read as re-sort, the anagram signal acting on BAD SUMMON.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official appointed to investigate complaints made by the public against organisations.

parts.note: not the harmonica but literally an organ of the body found in the mouth

explanation.walkthrough: A mouth organ is a harmonica, but the question mark invites reading it literally: a bodily organ located in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue is a muscular organ inside the mouth used for taste and speech.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: neat and smart in appearance

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a big spruce tree, but both words are separate meanings of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sizeable informally (a tidy sum of money) and also neat, orderly and smart.

indicators.note: missing its final letter, so the end of the word is cut off

parts.note: a crew is a team of people working together

explanation.surface: The crew missed their last meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a light afternoon or early evening meal in Britain.

indicators.note: to flounder is to struggle clumsily, so the letters stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A fishy scene: look at the cod, and there go the flounders.
explanation.walkthrough: With cod about, flounders reads as fish, but it is the verb signalling an anagram of COD I SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the district under a bishop's authority, which is also called a diocese.

indicators.note: dropped means left out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a mask is worn as a disguise
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Mike is questioned and his disguise is no longer used.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone is to ask them something; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Type of house built by a French girl in East End district

indicators.note: the French article and the girl sit in the district, so they go inside it

parts.note: Bow is a district in London's East End
un is French for a
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A house is being constructed by a French girl in a part of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: BOW is an area of the East End of London, traditionally home to Cockneys born within the sound of Bow Bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a style of single-storey house.

clue.text: Flourishing, the Duke of Milan and us

parts.note: Prospero is the deposed Duke of Milan in Shakespeare's The Tempest

explanation.surface: We and the Duke of Milan are doing well together.
explanation.walkthrough: Prospero is the magician of Shakespeare's The Tempest, the rightful Duke of Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperous means successful and thriving, especially financially.

clue.text: Technician's beginning to study surface of tyre

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A mechanic starts examining the surface of a tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: The tread is the grooved part of a tyre that touches the road.

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
R is a standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A relative stands beside a river on a misty day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazy is vague or indistinct, not clear.

clue.text: Female companion in timeless novel's beginning?

indicators.note: without time, so the letter standing for time is taken out

parts.note: a novel begins with chapter one

explanation.surface: A question of whether a woman's companion appears at the start of an ageless novel.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the usual abbreviation for time; drop it from CHAPTER ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone is traditionally an older woman accompanying a young unmarried woman in public.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to continue after a pause
second meaning: a brief written account; the question mark admits the stretch to a CV as a summary of one's life

explanation.walkthrough: Pronounced differently, one spelling gives both the verb meaning carry on and the noun for a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to restart something interrupted; a résumé is a brief account or summary.

clue.text: Savouries available in Greek island, for instance

parts.note: Samos is an island in the eastern Aegean
as means for example, as in cities such as Paris

explanation.surface: Tasty snacks can be had on a Greek island, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Samosas are fried pastry parcels with a spiced filling, savoury snacks from South Asian cuisine.

parts.note: someone who is concerned about something cares about it
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A parent worries about their son's pet animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a noun after son's, but it is the verb meaning to stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet is to stroke affectionately, which is a caress.

parts.note: to shut is to close

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the word's first letter is used

explanation.surface: A little cupboard whose door is shut tight.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a small room or cupboard for storage, chiefly in American usage.

indicators.note: tossed like a salad, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An oil worker flips a coin or banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal sum is a token one, very small and not reflecting real value.

parts.note: Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A spooky lake in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and frightening, the kind of atmosphere associated with spirits.

indicators.note: set free, so the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal resembling a badger will be released at a later time.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, is an African and Asian mammal related to badgers.

clue.text: English journalists inside like this coffee

indicators.note: inside means put within, so one word sits in the other

parts.note: so means in this way
the press is the collective term for journalists

explanation.surface: English reporters indoors enjoying this type of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A parent is visibly embarrassed about their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visually' makes the definition fair: an embarrassed person is seen to turn red in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed blushes, so they look red in the face.

indicators.note: the letter has to go, so it is removed from the word

parts.note: to have accepted something is to have took it
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: It is also agreed that the king must abdicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Too means as well or in addition.

parts.note: US stands for United States, so American

explanation.surface: An American newspaper editor was exploited.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone manipulated has been used, exploited for another person's ends.

clue.text: Is following order about right latticework

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece goes at the end
about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to tell someone to do something is to order them

explanation.surface: An instruction about a right-hand side follows, concerning a garden trellis.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a framework of crossed strips of wood used to support climbing plants.
